assumptions.choice: Spec requires the 4-hour (H4) chart, but the harness only supplies 1h bars on a single feed with no resampling access inside the strategy class. EMA(200) and SMA(60) are computed directly on the provided 1h feed rather than on reconstructed 4h bars.
assumptions.reason: No mechanism is available within a single bt.Strategy class (no cerebro access) to resample the fixed 1h feed into true 4h bars; applying the exact stated indicator periods to the only available feed is the closest literal reading.

assumptions.choice: Size each entry at 2% of current portfolio value (broker.getvalue() * 0.02 / close).
assumptions.reason: Spec states 'small position size (for example, 1-2% of total trading capital)' but gives no exact figure; 2% (upper end of the stated range) was chosen as a concrete rule.

assumptions.choice: Defined 'descending resistance' as Highest(high, 20) at retest time being lower than Highest(high, 20) taken 20 bars earlier, and 'broken' as close[0] > current 20-bar resistance high; both required for entry.
assumptions.reason: Spec recommends considering descending resistance and says a break makes entry 'more likely', but gives no lookback length or formal definition of descending/broken; a concrete 20-bar rolling-high comparison was chosen as the closest implementable literal reading.

assumptions.choice: Retest confirmed when the bar's range touches the EMA (low<=EMA<=high) AND either the candle is bullish (close>open) or the close is back above the EMA (bounce).
assumptions.reason: Spec gives 'bullish candlestick pattern' and 'price bounces off the EMA' as examples ('for example ... or') of support confirmation, read as alternative (OR) conditions.

assumptions.choice: Take-profit and stop-loss are evaluated against the bar's close price rather than intrabar high/low.
assumptions.reason: Spec does not specify intrabar execution; close-based checks are used consistently for both exit conditions as the simplest literal reading of 'price reaches'/'price falls'.

assumptions.choice: Kept the 'SMA unavailable -> 5% take-profit' branch as literally specified even though it is effectively unreachable, since EMA(200)'s automatic minperiod (200) always exceeds SMA(60)'s minperiod (60), so SMA is always valid once next() runs.
assumptions.reason: Fidelity to the explicitly stated fallback rule, despite it not being triggerable given backtrader's automatic warm-up alignment in this environment.
